mainTopic: Which fats are forbidden as חלב, which fats can seal a hole so the animal is not a טרפה, and the limits of 'the תורה cares about the money of ישראל.'
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא argue about which extra fat the פסוק forbids: the fat on the small intestines or the fat on the קבה. A second ברייתא seems to switch their views. רבי יוחנן says to reverse the names in the first ברייתא, because the second one gives exact reasoning ('מה... אף'). רב נחמן בר יצחק then explains that רבי ישמעאל only reported his forefathers' lenient practice and did not hold it himself. Next, רב and רב ששת argue whether forbidden fat can seal a hole in an organ so the animal is not a טרפה. אביי adds that the fat of a חיה does not seal, because it is not firmly attached. Two stories follow in which רבא rules leniently, partly because 'the תורה cares about the money of ישראל.' Each time he is challenged: first in a case of a תורה prohibition, then in a case of uncovered honey, which involves danger to life. The amud closes with rules about which fats seal: hat-shaped fat does not, and of the חימצא and the בר חימצא, only the בר חימצא seals. The גמרא then starts a proof of which fat is which, and that proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First ברייתא: which extra fat the פסוק includes
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says the extra words in the פסוק include the fat on the small intestines. רבי עקיבא says they include the fat on the קבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and all the fat...' This comes to include the fat on the small intestines; these are the words of רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says: it comes to include the fat on the קבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that reads extra words in the פסוק about forbidden fat. Two תנאים disagree about which additional fat those words include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא uses the extra word 'all' to add one more kind of fat to the list of forbidden חלב. רבי ישמעאל adds the fat on the small intestines. רבי עקיבא adds the fat on the קבה. As written here, רבי עקיבא's opinion forbids the fat of the קבה, and רבי ישמעאל's does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
'To bring in': a word in the פסוק includes another case
The small (thin) intestines
The abomasum, the fourth stomach of an animal

phrases.english: '...etc.' – to include the fat
phrases.notes: This is the end of a quoted פסוק (ויקרא 3:3). The extra word 'all' is what includes more fat.

phrases.english: that is on the small intestines,
these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says:
to include the fat that is on the abomasum.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהָבִיא חֵלֶב שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַדַּקִּין, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, the פסוק includes the fat on the small intestines. According to רבי עקיבא, it includes the fat on the קבה.

steps.title: A second ברייתא seems to flip the opinions
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא gives רבי שמעון a broad test that would forbid the fat of the קבה. It gives רבי עקיבא a narrower test that would permit it. This is the reverse of the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with this: 'The fat that is upon the innards.' רבי שמעון says: Just as the fat covering the innards has a membrane and peels off easily, so too all fat with a membrane that peels off is forbidden. רבי עקיבא says: Just as the fat covering the innards is spread loosely, has a membrane and peels off, so too all fat that is spread loosely, has a membrane and peels off is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that contradicts the first one about who holds what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, רבי שמעון (treated here as the opinion of רבי ישמעאל) needs only two signs: a membrane, and that it peels off. That test includes the fat of the קבה. רבי עקיבא adds a third sign: the fat must be spread loosely (תותב). The fat of the קבה is stuck on tightly, so his test leaves it out. So now רבי עקיבא is the stricter one about the קבה, the exact opposite of the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The innards, the inner organs
'Just as... so too': building a general rule from the example in the פסוק
A thin membrane covering the fat
Peels off easily
Spread out loosely on top, not fixed tightly

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get lost in the names. The key point is that in the first ברייתא רבי עקיבא forbids the fat of the קבה. In this second ברייתא, his extra condition (תותב) means he permits it. That switch is the contradiction.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
'The fat that is upon the innards' –
Rabbi Shimon says:
Just as the fat that covers the innards
has a membrane and peels off,
so too all fat with a membrane that peels off is forbidden.
Rabbi Akiva says:
Just as the fat that covers the innards
is spread loosely, has a membrane, and peels off,
so too all fat that is spread loosely, has a membrane, and peels off is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a second ברייתא against the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's report of who includes the fat of the קבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the second ברייתא, רבי עקיבא's extra condition (תותב) leaves out the fat of the קבה, while the other view's broader test includes it. That is the opposite of the first ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: reverse the names in the first ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבין sends a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: the second ברייתא has the correct order, so we switch the names in the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the correct layout of the teaching, and reverse the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by saying the names in the first ברייתא were switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we reverse the first ברייתא, רבי עקיבא includes the fat on the small intestines and רבי ישמעאל includes the fat of the קבה. Now both ברייתות agree: רבי ישמעאל is the one who forbids the fat of the קבה, and רבי עקיבא permits it.

keyTerms.meaning: The arrangement or layout of a teaching
Reverse, switch the names
The first one (here, the first ברייתא)

phrases.english: Ravin sent in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Such is the proper layout of the teaching,
phrases.notes: 'Teaching' here means the second ברייתא. Its order of names is the right one.

phrases.english: and reverse the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח רָבִין מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּךְ הִיא הַצָּעָה שֶׁל מִשְׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching the names (אוקימתא of the text by reversing the names)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות have the names right, so the תנאים contradict themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא's names are reversed: רבי ישמעאל forbids the fat of the קבה, and רבי עקיבא includes only the fat on the small intestines.

steps.title: Why reverse the first and not the second?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the choice: maybe we should reverse the second ברייתא instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you reverse the first one? Reverse the second one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's choice. Either ברייתא could have been switched, so why pick the first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Switching either ברייתא would remove the contradiction. If we switched the second one, רבי עקיבא would forbid the fat of the קבה instead. So the גמרא wants a reason for which version to trust.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What did you see?': why did you choose this option over the other?
The last (second) one

phrases.english: What did you see that you reversed the first one?
Reverse the second one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חָזֵית דְּאָפְכַתְּ קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's decision to reverse the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reversing the second ברייתא would fix the contradiction just as well, so there is no clear reason to prefer the first option.

steps.title: The second ברייתא gives exact reasoning, so it is reliable
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא uses the careful 'מה... אף' reasoning, so it is precise and its names should be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different: since it teaches 'just as', it is exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the second ברייתא is the one to trust.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא does more than give a ruling. It spells out the logic behind each view ('just as the fat on the innards has these signs...'). A teaching that is this careful about the reasoning is assumed to be careful about who said what too. So the first ברייתא is the one we reverse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here it is different': this case has a special feature
Exact, precise, meant carefully

steps.whatToRemember: The second ברייתא is trusted because it gives exact reasons (מה... אף). So the first ברייתא's names are switched. רבי ישמעאל forbids the fat of the קבה, and רבי עקיבא, who needs the fat to be תותב, permits it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule for fixing contradictions between ברייתות. A version that carefully explains its reasoning is treated as more exact than one that only states the rulings.

phrases.english: Here it is different,
since it teaches 'just as',
it is exact.
phrases.notes: He means: because the second ברייתא spells out its reasoning so carefully, we trust it on the names too.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָכָא, כֵּיוָן דְּקָתָנֵי ״מָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that one source is more precise than the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות are equally reliable, so either one could be switched.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ברייתא, with its careful 'מה' reasoning, is exact. So we reverse the first one.

steps.title: After the switch, the lenient view belongs to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: Now that the names in the first ברייתא are switched, the lenient view on the fat of the קבה belongs to רבי עקיבא. So how could רבי אושעיא say the כהנים acted like רבי ישמעאל?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, was it really like רבי ישמעאל? It is like רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem caused by switching the names in the first ברייתא. The lenient view, which the כהנים followed, now belongs to רבי עקיבא, not רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the switch, רבי ישמעאל only added the fat on the small intestines, so he permitted the fat of the קבה. After the switch, רבי ישמעאל is the one who forbids the fat of the קבה. That clashes with רבי אושעיא's statement that the כהנים permitted it 'like רבי ישמעאל'.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: a challenge built on the conclusion just reached
It is like רבי עקיבא, meaning it actually matches his view

phrases.english: If so, was it like Rabbi Yishmael?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי אושעיא's earlier statement that the כהנים permitted the fat of the קבה, like רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: It is like Rabbi Akiva!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out a problem that follows from accepting the name switch in steps 3 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's statement that the כהנים followed רבי ישמעאל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the names are switched, the lenient view on the fat of the קבה belongs to רבי עקיבא, so linking it to רבי ישמעאל seems wrong.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reported his forefathers' view but did not hold it
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that רבי ישמעאל said the lenient view in the name of his forefathers, but he himself did not agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבי אושעיא meant that רבי ישמעאל said this in the name of his forefathers, but he himself did not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge. When רבי אושעיא linked the practice to רבי ישמעאל, he meant only that רבי ישמעאל passed on the tradition, not that he agreed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the clash. The name switch can stay as it is, so רבי ישמעאל personally forbids the fat of the קבה. The lenient practice was a tradition of his forefathers, which he reported but did not follow.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of his forefathers: passing on a family tradition
He does not hold this view himself

steps.whatToRemember: With the names switched, רבי ישמעאל himself forbids the fat of the קבה. The lenient practice of the כהנים was only a tradition he reported from his forefathers.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
[He meant] that he said it in the name of his forefathers,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ישמעאל, who was himself a כהן. He was passing on what his family taught.

phrases.english: but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם אֲבוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the attribution: רבי ישמעאל was quoting a view he did not hold himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רבי ישמעאל personally permitted the fat of the קבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל only reported his forefathers' lenient tradition. He himself forbids the fat of the קבה.

steps.title: Does fat seal a hole in the innards?
steps.stepSummary: רב says permitted fat seals a hole and forbidden fat does not. רב ששת says both kinds of fat seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: permitted fat seals a hole, and forbidden fat does not seal. רב ששת says: both this kind and that kind seal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic that links the laws of fats to טרפות. רב and רב ששת disagree about which fat can seal a hole in the innards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an organ has a hole, the animal can become a טרפה. If fat covering the hole counts as a seal, the animal stays kosher. רב says only permitted fat works as a seal, while רב ששת says forbidden fat works too.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted fat, which may be eaten
Forbidden fat, which may not be eaten
Seals: closes a hole so the animal does not become a טרפה
An animal with a fatal defect, which is forbidden to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Here טהור and טמא do not mean pure and impure (טומאה). They mean fat that is permitted to eat and fat that is forbidden (חלב).

phrases.english: Rav said: Permitted fat seals [a hole],
phrases.notes: He means a hole in the innards that the fat covers. If the fat seals it, the animal does not become a טרפה.

phrases.english: forbidden [fat] does not seal.
And Rav Sheshet says:
Both this and that seal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: חֵלֶב טָהוֹר – סוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about fats and טרפות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: only permitted fat seals a hole. רב ששת: both permitted and forbidden fat seal.

steps.title: Does the fat of a wild animal seal?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about the fat of a חיה. All of it is permitted to eat, so does it seal according to רב? Or did רב's rule depend on the fat being firmly attached, which this fat is not?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: what is the law for the fat of a חיה? Did רב mean exactly that permitted fat seals, and this fat is also permitted? Or perhaps permitted fat seals because it is firmly attached, and this fat is not firmly attached?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא raises a question about רב's rule. He wants to know the reason permitted fat seals, so he can tell whether the fat of a חיה also seals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible reasons behind רב's rule. One reason is simply that the fat is permitted, and the fat of a חיה is all permitted. The other reason is that permitted fat sticks tightly to the organ. The fat of a חיה does not stick tightly, so under that reason it would not seal.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises a question that has no clear answer yet
The fat of a wild animal, all of which is permitted to eat
Exactly, precisely as stated
Is firmly attached, sticks tightly

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
The fat of a wild animal, what [is the law]?
phrases.notes: With a חיה, even the fat on the innards is permitted to eat.

phrases.english: Did he say exactly that permitted fat seals,
and this too is permitted [so it seals],
or perhaps [it seals] because it is firmly attached,
and this is not firmly attached?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: חֵלֶב חַיָּה מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רב's rule from step 8 applies to the fat of a חיה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason permitted fat seals that it is permitted, or that it is firmly attached? The answer decides whether the fat of a חיה seals.

steps.title: אביי: wild animal fat is permitted but still does not seal
steps.stepSummary: אביי says there is nothing to ask. The fat of a חיה may be permitted to eat, but it is not firmly attached, so it does not seal.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: why is he asking this? Granted, the fat is permitted to eat, but it is still not firmly attached.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי זירא's question and says the answer is obvious. Being permitted to eat does not make fat a seal; what counts is being firmly attached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats the attachment as the real reason behind רב's rule. The fat of a חיה is permitted, but it does not stick tightly to the organ. So it cannot seal a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Why is he asking this? The answer is obvious
Granted that, even though
Permitted to eat

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, fat seals a hole because it is firmly attached, not because it is permitted to eat. So the fat of a חיה does not seal.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Why does he ask this?
Granted that it is permitted to eat,
[but] it is not firmly attached at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fat of a חיה does not seal, because it is not firmly attached, even though it is permitted to eat.

steps.title: רבא permits a hole sealed by forbidden fat
steps.stepSummary: A case came to רבא of a hole sealed by forbidden fat. He permitted it for two reasons: רב ששת holds forbidden fat also seals, and the תורה cares about Jewish money.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a hole sealed by forbidden fat that came before רבא. רבא said: What should we worry about? First, רב ששת said forbidden fat also seals. Also, the תורה cares about the money of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that puts the argument between רב and רב ששת from Step 8 into practice. רבא rules leniently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has two supports. First, there is an opinion (רב ששת) that forbidden fat seals the hole. Second, he adds a general idea: the תורה does not want Jews to lose money for no reason, so we can lean toward the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: A hole in one of the animal's organs, which can make it a טריפה
What should we worry about here? A way of saying there is no real problem

keyTerms.term: הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
keyTerms.meaning: The תורה cares about the money of ישראל and does not want them to lose it needlessly

phrases.english: A certain hole that was sealed by forbidden fat
that came before Rava.
Rava said: What should we worry about?
First, because Rav Sheshet said:
Forbidden fat also seals,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד – הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and also, the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא נֶקֶב דְּסַתְמֵהּ חֵלֶב טָמֵא, דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the רב and רב ששת argument from Step 8 to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא permits the animal: forbidden fat seals according to רב ששת, and the תורה cares about Jewish money.

steps.title: רב פפא objects: you cannot rely on money in a Torah prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges רבא: רב says forbidden fat does not seal, and this is a תורה prohibition, so how can you use 'the תורה cares about money'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: There is רב's opinion, and this is a תורה prohibition, and you say 'the תורה cares about the money of ישראל'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא attacks רבא's second reason. He says that idea cannot outweigh a real opinion when the question is a תורה prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a real argument here: רב forbids and רב ששת permits. When the question is about a prohibition from the תורה itself, we cannot simply pick the lenient side to save money. Caring about money is not a reason to risk breaking a תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition from the תורה itself, not just a rabbinic rule

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the idea of 'the תורה cares about money' is false. He is saying it cannot be used to decide an argument about a תורה prohibition.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
There is Rav's opinion, and it is a Torah prohibition,
phrases.notes: He means: רב holds forbidden fat does not seal (Step 8), and eating a טריפה is forbidden by the תורה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ ״הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל״?!
phrases.english: and you say 'the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: רַב, וְאִיסּוּרָא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of 'the תורה cares about Jewish money' to rule leniently.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When there is a real opinion (רב) that it is forbidden by the תורה, saving money is not a good enough reason to be lenient.

steps.title: רבא permits an uncovered jug of honey
steps.stepSummary: מניומין the jug maker had a jug of honey left uncovered. רבא permitted it: the משנה lists only wine, water, and milk as forbidden when uncovered, and the תורה cares about Jewish money.
steps.simpleTranslation: מניומין the jug maker had a jug of honey that was left uncovered. He came before רבא. רבא said: What should we worry about? First, the משנה says: Three liquids are forbidden because of being uncovered: wine, water, and milk, and all other liquids are allowed. Also, the תורה cares about the money of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story in the same pattern. Again רבא permits with the same two kinds of reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with uncovered liquids is that a snake may have drunk from them and left poison. רבא points out that the משנה lists only three liquids as a concern, and honey is not one of them. He again adds that the תורה cares about Jewish money.

keyTerms.meaning: Being left uncovered, which raises a worry that a snake drank from it and left poison
A jug
Honey
Liquids

phrases.english: Manyumin the jug maker
had a jug of honey that was left uncovered,
he came before Rava.
Rava said: What should we worry about?
First, as we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in תרומות 8:4.

phrases.english: Three liquids are forbidden because of being uncovered:
wine, water, and milk,
and all other liquids are allowed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד – הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and also, the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְיוֹמִין כַּנְדּוּקָא אִיגַּלִּי לֵיהּ בֻּסְתְּקָא דְּדוּבְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story where רבא uses the same 'money' reasoning in a new area.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncovered honey is permitted: only wine, water, and milk are forbidden when uncovered, and the תורה cares about Jewish money.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects: you cannot rely on money when life is in danger
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רבא: רבי שמעון forbids honey, and this is a danger to life, so how can you rely on 'the תורה cares about money'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: There is רבי שמעון's opinion, and this is a danger to life, and you say 'the תורה cares about the money of ישראל'?
steps.whatsHappening: Just like רב פפא before, רב נחמן בר יצחק attacks רבא's money reason. This time the issue is danger to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an opinion, רבי שמעון, that honey is also a concern when uncovered. When life may be in danger, we are stricter than with a regular prohibition. So saving money cannot be the reason to ignore a stricter opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A danger to life

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
There is Rabbi Shimon's opinion, and it is a danger to life,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ ״הַתּוֹרָה חָסָה עַל מָמוֹנָם שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל״?
phrases.english: and you say 'the Torah cares about the money of the Jewish people'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְסַכָּנַת נְפָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in Step 13, the same way Step 12 challenged Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of 'the תורה cares about Jewish money' to permit uncovered honey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When there is a real opinion (רבי שמעון) that it is dangerous, saving money cannot justify the risk.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי שמעון's opinion about uncovered liquids comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the opinion of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask what רבי שמעון actually said. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק mentioned רבי שמעון without explaining. Before going on, the גמרא wants to show the source.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? A question asking for the source or details

phrases.english: What is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion used in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source and content of רבי שמעון's opinion about uncovered liquids.

steps.title: The ברייתא: five liquids, and רבי שמעון's snake
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says five liquids, including honey, have no problem of being uncovered. רבי שמעון disagrees and says he saw a snake drink fish brine. The חכמים answer that it was an odd snake.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: Five liquids have no problem of being uncovered: fish brine, vinegar, oil, honey, and fish sauce. רבי שמעון says: These also have the problem of being uncovered. רבי שמעון said: I saw a snake drink fish brine in צידן. They said to him: That snake was strange, and we do not bring proof from strange ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. It shows that רבי שמעון forbids even the five liquids, including honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say snakes do not drink these five liquids, so they are safe. רבי שמעון brings a story from his own eyes to show snakes do drink them. The חכמים reject his proof, saying one odd snake does not show how snakes normally act.

keyTerms.meaning: Fish brine, the salty liquid from fish
A fish sauce made from brine mixed with oil
Strange or crazy, acting not like others of its kind
We do not bring proof from strange cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון's strict view really does include honey, which is why רב נחמן בר יצחק used it against רבא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: חֲמִשָּׁה אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי:
phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Five liquids have no problem of being uncovered:
fish brine, vinegar, oil, honey, and fish sauce.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף הֵן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: These too have the problem of being uncovered.
And Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי רָאִיתִי נָחָשׁ שֶׁשָּׁתָה צִיר בְּצַיְדָּן.
phrases.english: I saw a snake that drank fish brine in Tzaidan.
They said to him: That one was strange,
and we do not bring proof from strange ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: חֲמִשָּׁה אֵין בָּהֶם מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון, in a ברייתא, holds that even fish brine, vinegar, oil, honey, and fish sauce are forbidden when uncovered.

steps.title: רבא: at least agree with me about fish brine
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נחמן בר יצחק: at least agree that the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון about fish brine, since the חכמים used to pour uncovered liquids into brine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: At least agree with me about fish brine. For רב פפא, רב הונא the son of רב יהושע, and the חכמים, when they had an uncovered liquid, would throw it into fish brine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back. He brings a practice of the חכמים to show that we do not follow רבי שמעון, at least about fish brine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים threw uncovered liquids into fish brine, because its sharpness cancels the poison. So clearly they did not worry that brine itself is dangerous, against רבי שמעון. רבא's point is that if we do not follow רבי שמעון for brine, we should not follow him for honey either.

keyTerms.meaning: Agree with me, admit to me
At least
They threw, they poured

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹדִי לִי מִיהַת בְּצִיר,
phrases.english: Rava said to him: At least agree with me about fish brine,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: because Rav Pappa, Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua, and the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה לְהוּ גִּילּוּיָא, שָׁדוּ לֵיהּ בְּצִיר.
phrases.english: when they had an uncovered liquid, would throw it into fish brine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹדִי לִי מִיהַת בְּצִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers the challenge of Step 14 by showing the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון in at least one of his cases.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון about fish brine, and so probably not about honey either.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רב פפא, רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, and the חכמים of throwing uncovered liquids into brine.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: at least agree with me about honey
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers: at least agree about honey, since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also forbids uncovered honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: At least agree with me about honey, because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds like רבי שמעון. As a ברייתא teaches: And so too רבי שמעון בן אלעזר would forbid honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers רבא's point. Brine may be different, but honey has a second תנא who forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא tried to say: since we do not follow רבי שמעון about brine, we should not follow him about honey. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that honey is stronger, because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees with רבי שמעון there. So with honey, a danger to life, we cannot just rely on 'the תורה cares about money.'

keyTerms.meaning: Holds like him, agrees with his opinion
Forbids

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories teach the same lesson: 'the תורה cares about the money of ישראל' cannot outweigh a real opinion that forbids, when the issue is a תורה prohibition or a danger to life. For uncovered honey, רבי שמעון and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר both forbid it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹדִי לִי מִיהָא בִּדְבַשׁ,
phrases.english: He said to him: At least agree with me about honey,

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר קָאֵי כְּוָותֵיהּ,
phrases.english: because Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds like him,
as it was taught in a baraita: And so too

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹסֵר בִּדְבַשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would forbid honey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אוֹדִי לִי מִיהָא בִּדְבַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's argument from Step 17 and keeps the challenge of Step 14 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes honey from fish brine by showing a second תנא supports the strict view for honey.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון about brine, it is not like him about honey either.
steps.terutzMaskana: Honey is different, because רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also forbids it, so the strict view there carries real weight.

steps.title: Fat shaped like a hat does not seal a hole
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that fat shaped like a hat does not seal a hole in the organ it covers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Fat that is shaped like a hat does not seal a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of fat that sits on an organ and might plug a hole in it. רב נחמן teaches that fat shaped like a hat does not count as a seal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, fat that is stuck tightly to an organ can close up a hole, so the animal is not a טריפה. רב נחמן says hat-shaped fat is different. It only sits loosely over the organ like a cap, so it does not really plug the hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a hat. It sits over the organ like a cap.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Fat that is shaped like a hat
phrases.notes: He means fat that is allowed to be eaten, lying on an organ, not the forbidden kind of fat.

phrases.english: does not seal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: חֵלֶב הֶעָשׂוּי כְּכוֹבַע אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic of uncovered liquids and returns to the main topic of fats sealing holes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hat-shaped fat does not count as a seal over a hole.

steps.title: Where is this hat-shaped fat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where in the animal this hat-shaped fat is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is this fat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: which fat is רב נחמן talking about? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן gave a rule but did not say which part of the animal it is about. To use the rule, we need to know where this fat is.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: Where?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the location of the fat in רב נחמן's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which fat in the animal is the hat-shaped fat that does not seal.

steps.title: Two views: fat on the rectum or the membrane of the heart
steps.stepSummary: One view says it is the grains of fat on the rectum. Another view says it is the membrane around the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it is the grains of fat on the rectum, and some say it is the membrane of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two different answers about where the hat-shaped fat is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both places are organs where a hole makes the animal a טריפה. The two views disagree about which fat רב נחמן meant. Either way, that fat cannot save the animal by covering a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: The rectum, the last part of the intestines.
The membrane (thin covering) around the heart.

phrases.english: Some say: the grains of fat on the rectum,
and some say: the membrane of the heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לַהּ: חִיטֵּי דְּכַרְכְּשָׁא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: טַרְפְּשָׁא דְּלִיבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of where the fat is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either the grains of fat on the rectum or the membrane of the heart.

steps.title: רבא forgot which of two fats seals
steps.stepSummary: רבא heard from רב נחמן that of two fats, the חימצא and the בר חימצא, one seals and one does not, but he does not remember which.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I heard two things from רב נחמן about the חימצא and the בר חימצא. One seals and one does not seal, but I don't know which is which.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reports a teaching from רב נחמן about two fats on the קיבה, but admits he forgot which fat seals. This opens a new question for the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two fats with almost the same name, the חימצא and the בר חימצא. רבא remembers that only one of them can plug a hole, but not which one. The next steps try to fill in what he forgot.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of one fat on the קיבה (stomach).
'Son of חימצא,' the name of a second fat on the קיבה.
Seals a hole (Aramaic form of סותם).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן תַּרְתֵּי,
phrases.english: Rava said: I heard two things from Rav Nachman,
about the ḥimtza and the bar ḥimtza,
phrases.notes: These are two fats found on the stomach (קיבה), in different spots.

phrases.english: one seals and one does not seal,
but I don't know which of them is which.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from רב נחמן about fats that seal, this time on the קיבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Of the חימצא and the בר חימצא, one seals and one does not, but רבא did not remember which.

steps.title: The בר חימצא seals, the חימצא does not
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן say the בר חימצא seals and the חימצא does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא, son of רב נחמן, said: The בר חימצא seals; the חימצא does not seal.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים fill in what רבא forgot. They say the בר חימצא is the one that seals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles רבא's doubt. One of these sages is רב נחמן's own son, so he would know his father's teaching.

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: and Rav Huna, son of Rav Nachman, said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּר חִימְצָא סָתֵים, חִימְצָא לָא סָתֵים.
phrases.english: The bar ḥimtza seals; the ḥimtza does not seal.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: בַּר חִימְצָא סָתֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what רבא forgot.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בר חימצא seals and the חימצא does not.

steps.title: A memory sign: the son is stronger than the father
steps.stepSummary: רב טבות gives a way to remember the rule: the son is stronger than the father, so the 'son' fat (בר חימצא) is the one that seals.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טבות said: Your memory sign is: the power of the son is greater than the power of the father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב טבות gives a simple trick to remember which fat seals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר חימצא means 'son of חימצא.' The saying 'the son is stronger than the father' reminds us that the 'son' fat is the strong one that can seal a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: Your sign. A memory trick to help remember a rule.
The power of the son is greater than the power of the father.

steps.whatToRemember: The בר חימצא seals a hole and the חימצא does not. Remember it with: 'the son is stronger than the father.'

phrases.english: Rav Tavot said: And your memory sign is:
The power of the son is greater than the power of the father.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבוּת: וְסִימָנָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory trick for the ruling in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory trick: the 'son' fat (בר חימצא) is the stronger one that seals.

steps.title: Which fat is the חימצא and which is the בר חימצא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which actual fat on the קיבה is called חימצא and which is called בר חימצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is the חימצא and which one is the בר חימצא?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the בר חימצא seals, the גמרא asks which fat in the animal each name refers to. This sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the rule does not help unless we can find the right fat on the animal. So the גמרא now needs to match each name to a real place on the קיבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one?

phrases.english: Which is the ḥimtza and which is the bar ḥimtza?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי חִימְצָא וְהֵי בַּר חִימְצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the rule is settled, asks how to identify each fat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which fat on the קיבה is the חימצא and which is the בר חימצא.

steps.title: Starting a proof from another statement of רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof from a statement of רב נחמן about people eating one of the fats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רב נחמן said: They eat it...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing a proof to identify the fats, using another statement of רב נחמן. The statement goes on past this point, so this step only sets up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן talks about a group of people who eat one of these fats. The idea is that knowing which fat people treat as permitted to eat may show us which one is called which. The full argument comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: They actually eat it.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav Nachman said:
They eat it,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the people of ארץ ישראל. רב נחמן's sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אִינְהוּ מֵיכָל אָכְלִי
